title: Lecture 3 - Summations & Recurrence MCQs
description: Midterm MCQs on concepts, mathematical reasoning and proof steps. No code tracing or code-analysis questions.
subject: Algorithm Analysis

questions.question: What is Σ(i=1..n) 1?
questions.explanation: The constant 1 is added n times.

questions.question: What is 1+2+...+n?
questions.explanation: This is the arithmetic-series formula with n terms.

questions.question: What is the tight growth of Σ(i=1..n) i²?
questions.explanation: The exact sum n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 has a cubic leading term.

questions.question: What is the tight growth of Σ(i=1..n) i³?
questions.explanation: The sum equals [n(n+1)/2]², whose leading degree is four.

questions.question: How many terms occur in Σ(i=m..n) c when m≤n?
questions.explanation: Both endpoints are included.

questions.question: For fixed a>1, what is Σ(i=0..h) a^i?
questions.explanation: There are h+1 terms starting with a⁰, giving the standard geometric sum.

questions.question: Why does a triangular total n(n+1)/2 still have quadratic growth?
options: Division by 2 makes every polynomial linear.
Its leading term is n²/2; a constant factor does not change the growth class.
A triangular total has logarithmically many terms.
questions.correctAnswer: Its leading term is n²/2; a constant factor does not change the growth class.
questions.explanation: Expanding gives (n²+n)/2, which is Θ(n²).

questions.question: What information is needed in addition to a recurrence rule to terminate its expansion?
options: A base-case value or constant-cost base condition.
questions.correctAnswer: A base-case value or constant-cost base condition.
questions.explanation: The expansion stops when the remaining problem reaches its base case.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] For T(n)=T(n-1)+c, what is the correct k-step expansion before the base case?
questions.explanation: Each expansion subtracts one from the input and adds one c.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] With base T(1)=1, when does T(n-k) reach the base?
questions.explanation: Solve n-k=1.

questions.question: If T(1)=1 and T(n)=T(n-1)+c with fixed c>0, what is T(n)?
options: c log₂ n, hence Θ(log n)
questions.explanation: There are n-1 non-base additions of c, then the base cost 1.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] For T(1)=1 and T(n)=T(n-1)+n, which sum is obtained?
questions.explanation: The non-recursive costs decrease by one at each expansion.

questions.question: What is the tight solution of T(n)=T(n-1)+n with T(1)=1?
questions.explanation: The expansion is the arithmetic sum n(n+1)/2.

questions.question: With constant positive base cost, what is T(n)=T(n/2)+c for fixed c>0?
questions.explanation: The problem halves at each step, giving logarithmic depth and constant work per level.

questions.question: With constant positive base cost, what is T(n)=T(n/2)+n?
questions.explanation: The work sums as n+n/2+n/4+..., a geometric series bounded by a constant multiple of n.

questions.question: With constant positive base cost, what is T(n)=2T(n/2)+1?
questions.explanation: A full binary recursion tree has Θ(n) nodes when its n leaves have constant size.

questions.question: For T(n)=2T(n/2)+cn, how many nodes are at level i if the root is level 0?
questions.explanation: Every node creates two children, so each level doubles the node count.

questions.question: For T(n)=2T(n/2)+cn, what is each node's input size at level i?
questions.explanation: Each level halves the size from the preceding level.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Which expression is the total non-recursive work at level i for T(n)=2T(n/2)+cn?
questions.explanation: Multiply the number of nodes by the cost per node; the powers cancel.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] For n a power of 2 and leaves of size 1, which equation gives the tree height?
questions.explanation: Repeated halving reaches 1 after log₂ n edges.

questions.question: For T(n)=2T(n/2)+cn with T(1)=Θ(1), what is the combined leaf cost?
questions.explanation: There are n leaves and each costs Θ(1).

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] Why is T(n)=2T(n/2)+cn in Θ(n log n)?
options: There are log₂ n internal levels costing cn each, plus Θ(n) leaf work.
The n leaves imply the entire tree must cost Θ(n).
There are n levels with n² work each.
questions.correctAnswer: There are log₂ n internal levels costing cn each, plus Θ(n) leaf work.
questions.explanation: Summing all levels gives cn log₂ n+Θ(n), not merely the leaf cost.

questions.question: [Proof MCQ] What distinguishes the substitution method from merely guessing a recurrence solution?
options: It assumes the answer without inequalities.
It eliminates the need for a base case.
It verifies the guessed bound using induction and base cases.
questions.correctAnswer: It verifies the guessed bound using induction and base cases.
questions.explanation: A guessed class becomes a proof only after the inductive inequality and starting cases are justified.

questions.question: Which recurrence models standard merge sort with linear merging?
questions.explanation: It sorts both halves and combines them with linear work.

questions.question: Why is the standard array merge sort in this lecture not constant-auxiliary-space?
options: Its recursion stack must contain n² frames.
Temporary arrays require Θ(n) peak space, dominating its logarithmic stack.
Every Θ(n log n) algorithm necessarily uses Θ(n log n) space.
questions.correctAnswer: Temporary arrays require Θ(n) peak space, dominating its logarithmic stack.
questions.explanation: The extra arrays, not just the stack depth, determine the auxiliary-space order.
